corrected_claim: The 2026 war was the US-Iran (US-Israel-Iran) conflict over the Strait of Hormuz, escalating around late Feb-Mar 2026, not a bilateral India-Pakistan war. Trump announced a two-week pause/ceasefire deal for Iran on 8 April 2026 (Asian markets surged that day; Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif brokered a proposed 'Islamabad Accord' peace initiative). Nifty traded roughly 23,000-24,800 during the war window; the specific 'Nifty closed ~24,000 on ceasefire day' and 'range 23,000-24,600 since April 8' could not be confirmed.

corrected_claim: The 14.7% unemployment / 20.5 million jobs lost figures came from the US jobs report released on Friday 8 May 2020 (April 2020 data), not the 3 April 2020 release. The 3 April 2020 release (March 2020 data) showed unemployment rising to 4.4% and nonfarm payrolls falling by 701,000. Despite the catastrophic May 8 data, US equities ended higher that day (widely reported rally), so a 'Dow fell only about 300' reaction is incorrect.

corrected_claim: Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini was born 17 May 1900 (some sources: 24 September 1902) and died 3 June 1989 - he was about 77-79 years old at the 1979 Iranian Revolution, not 45-46, and he died in 1989 (so he is not 'now 86'). He led the revolution that overthrew Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi; Iran's post-revolution oil-export disruption contributed to the 1979-80 oil crisis (Iran did not literally halt all shipments through the Strait of Hormuz).

corrected_claim: The Kargil War was fought between India and Pakistan from May to July 1999 (Operation Vijay). A ~5-6% Nifty fall specifically during the war could not be confirmed; verifiable context: from the end of the war until February 2000 the Indian stock market rose by more than 30%, and the dot-com boom coincided with the period.

corrected_claim: The 2008 global financial crisis crash was far deeper than ~30%: Nifty fell roughly 60-64% from its January 2008 peak (~6,287 intraday) to its October 2008 trough (~2,252-2,520), and the Sensex fell ~63% (intraday peak 21,078 on 8 Jan 2008 to intraday low 7,697.39 on 27 Oct 2008). The ~30% drawdown figure matches the 2004 correction more closely; the 2020 COVID crash was ~38% (Nifty ~12,430 to ~7,611).

evidence.title: Wikipedia - BSE SENSEX (2008 peak 21,078 / Oct 27 2008 intraday low 7,697.39)
Wikipedia - Stock market crashes in India (Crashes of 2008 section)

notes: 'Nifty fell ~30% in 2008' is materially wrong; corrected to ~60%+ peak-to-trough.

corrected_claim: The COVID-19 second wave (March-May 2021) saw Nifty correct from about 15,200 to roughly 14,100-14,200 (-7% or so in April 2021) - nowhere near 7,000-8,000. The 7,000-8,000 levels were the FIRST-wave crash in March 2020: Nifty closed at 7,610.25 on 23 March 2020 and fell to intraday lows around 7,500 (all-time low print ~7,511 on 24 Mar 2020).

evidence.title: Wikipedia - Stock market crashes in India (Crashes of 2020 section: Nifty 7,610.25 close on 23 Mar 2020)

notes: Confused first-wave (Mar 2020) and second-wave (Apr-May 2021) crashes; second wave never approached 7,000-8,000.
